_comment: Class-level priors for the GTA VI trophy forecast (data/priors.json). main.py classifies each trophy from its own description at run time and shrinks its fitted growth curve toward its class prior. These are judgement priors about how fast different kinds of trophies are earned in a launch week, stated two ways: prior_slope, the exponent b in earners(t) ~ (1 + t)^b used only when the history is too thin to fit a curve at all; and prior_tau_hours, the time constant of the saturating curve earners(t) ~ 1 - exp(-t/tau) that the main fit shrinks toward (story trophies saturate in about a day, grinds take most of the week, the platinum essentially never arrives). They are NOT per-trophy forecasts: every trophy's level is anchored on its own last observed rate, and the fitted curve from the case history dominates whenever the history is informative (prior weight = 6 reads).

caps.note: The tracked-player fit is a saturating curve; total growth is capped at 10x the last read, so a noisy early fit cannot explode the denominator.

activity.note: One-off activities and feats (win a race, beat a challenge, rob a bank/vault, explore the map, spend money, discover vehicles). Mid-speed: reachable in normal play, but not every player attempts each one.

collectible.note: Exploration collectibles (meditate at every spot, card sets, every location). Slow: completionists only, late in the week.

grind.note: Count-based grinds (250 stunts, 50 challenges, 100 locations, 3 card sets, 100% completion). Cumulative earners grow slowly: the count takes many hours even for dedicated players.

platinum.note: Platinum needs everything else first; essentially nobody earns it in week one. Earner growth is barely above flat.

story.note: Main-story progress (chapters, finale, named story missions). The bulk of the launch-week player base pushes through the story, so cumulative earners rise steeply in the first day and then level off as the story-playing cohort is exhausted.

strand.note: Side-strand finales (final mission for a named stranger/contact). Slower than the main story: only players who seek the strand out reach its end in week one.

classify.activity: everything else: one-off feats, wins, robberies, purchases, money goals
classify.collectible: description is about finding/doing something at every spot/location across the map (meditate at every spot, WAiNK at 100 locations, discover vehicles, explore all of Leonida)
classify.grind: description contains a count to complete (250 Stunts, 50 Challenges, 100 locations, 3 sets) or is 'Attain 100% Completion' or 'Earn a gold medal in all ... challenges'
classify.story: description starts with 'Complete Chapter' or 'Complete the final mission.' or matches 'Complete <named story mission>.' (a named mission that is not a finale for a person)
classify.strand: description matches 'Complete the final mission for <name>.'

spread.note: Spread is combined in quadrature on the logit scale: the per-trophy fit residual, a model-error term growing with the horizon (no functional form is the truth, and the launch weekend sits inside the horizon), a fixed refresh-shock term (Exophase refreshes its counts in lumps, hours apart, and the answer is the page as of its last refresh before the target), and a staleness term when the last read is unchanged for hours. There is no random-walk term: the median is a trend extrapolation, not a random walk from the last value, so its uncertainty is the trend's, not a walk's.
